name: Cynthia (Cinde) Wirth
gradeNote: Wirth has no legislative record; in a 2024 WFYI interview she backed Congress enshrining abortion protections, calling abortion "a health care procedure," and supported stronger gun background checks, and a Take Back Congress profile lists "protecting reproductive freedom" in her platform. She did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates her Liberal from public data, and her listed endorsements include the AFL-CIO and Progressive Voters Network.
description: Columbus-based small-business owner, scientist and former public high school biology teacher who was the 2024 Democratic nominee against Shreve.

name: Jefferson Shreve
gradeNote: Shreve holds an A+ from SBA Pro-Life America, which endorsed his re-election, and a 96% Heritage Action score for the 119th Congress; his platform includes abortion restrictions, gun rights, border security and reduced spending. As a 2023 Indianapolis mayoral candidate he proposed ending permitless carry, raising the gun-purchase age to 21 and banning assault-weapon sales in Marion County, a departure from the GOP line on the Second Amendment.
description: First-term Republican congressman, self-storage business founder and former Indianapolis City-County councilor who ran unsuccessfully for Indianapolis mayor in 2023.

name: André Carson
gradeNote: Carson holds an F from SBA Pro-Life America, which says he has consistently voted against protections for the unborn and children born alive after failed abortions, and a 0% Heritage Action score for the 119th Congress (7% lifetime). He voted Yea on final passage of the Respect for Marriage Act (Roll Call 513, Dec. 8, 2022).
description: Democratic congressman representing Indianapolis since a 2008 special election, Indiana's longest-serving current U.S. House member.

name: Patrick McAuley
gradeNote: McAuley has no voting record, and his campaign issues page covers only public safety, housing and job training; in a WFYI interview he called federal appropriations "a mess," proposed cutting overlapping humanitarian aid accounts and supported voter ID, while saying he is "completely open" to immigrants and criticizing ICE tactics. No public positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or guns were found, and iVoterGuide lists him as Insufficient Information.
description: Republican nominee who works in commercial real estate and previously interned for U.S. Sen. Todd Young.

name: James M Sceniak
gradeNote: Sceniak told WFYI he wants lower taxes for individuals, backs the "Penny Plan" to trim federal budgets and calls inflation a tax, while describing a welcoming "Reagan" view on immigration. He did not answer iVoterGuide's questions on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns, and iVoterGuide rates him Moderate.
description: Libertarian behavior therapist and repeat congressional candidate (2022 U.S. Senate, 2024 6th District) with no campaign website.

name: Mary Allen
gradeNote: Allen has no federal record; her campaign priorities call for the wealthy and corporations to "pay their fair share in taxes," more funding for USAID and public schools, opposition to dismantling the Department of Education, and immigration pathways to citizenship. She did not answer iVoterGuide's questions on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns, and iVoterGuide rates her Liberal from public data.
description: At-large Evansville City Council member, small-business owner, Army Reserve veteran and former occupational therapist.

name: Mark Messmer
gradeNote: Messmer holds an A+ from SBA Pro-Life America for votes including defunding Planned Parenthood through H.R. 1, and a 96% Heritage Action score for the 119th Congress. As Indiana Senate majority leader in 2022 he voted against SB 1, the near-total abortion ban, in committee, saying every anti-abortion organization he talked to had urged a no vote.
description: First-term Republican congressman from Jasper, small-business owner, and former Indiana Senate majority leader and state representative.

name: Brad A. Meyer
gradeNote: Meyer has no legislative record; his campaign advocates Medicare for All and stronger collective bargaining, and he told the Capital Chronicle he would make the first $20,000 in wages tax-free. He did not answer any iVoterGuide questions, which rates him Liberal from public data, and his listed endorsements include the AFL-CIO and Progressive Voters Network.
description: Democratic nominee and Bloomington electronics engineer whose career includes manufacturing and civilian engineering work for the U.S. Navy.

name: Erin Houchin
gradeNote: Houchin holds an A+ from SBA Pro-Life America, which notes she introduced the Abortion Funding Awareness Act and voted to defund Planned Parenthood through H.R. 1, and a 94% Heritage Action score for the 119th Congress (80% lifetime). Her platform emphasizes border security, reduced federal spending, abortion restrictions and parental involvement in education.
description: Republican congresswoman from Salem seeking a third term, a former Indiana state senator.

name: Tonya L. Hudson
gradeNote: In iVoterGuide answers Hudson agreed human life deserves legal protection from conception, strongly opposed taxpayer funding for abortion providers, opposed any new gun restrictions, opposed compelling businesses to provide services against their beliefs, and backed spending cuts, a balanced budget and abolishing the IRS. She strongly disagreed with defining marriage as one man and one woman and said anyone not dangerous should be allowed to migrate, though her campaign site calls for securing the southern border.
description: Libertarian real estate broker from Mitchell who previously ran for the 9th District seat in 2020 and 2022 and for lieutenant governor.
